start.tagline: runs in your browser · no account · STL and 3MF
start.title: What are you printing?

box.desc: Bin or tray on the Gridfinity grid, with lip, scoop and dividers.

baseplate.desc: Grid plate for your bins. Magnets, screws, split to fit your bed.

cutout.desc: Bin with a pocket shaped to your tool. Import an STL or use a simple shape.

keychainImage.desc: Relief keychain from a picture: a drawing, logo or emblem becomes a silhouette with a height pattern.

keychainShape.desc: A plain tag from a ready-made shape: rectangle, circle, ellipse, capsule or polygon, with an optional rim.

lip.title: Lip
lip.help: The lip is the rim at the top of the bin that mates with the foot of a bin stacked above it. None gives a flat top. The lip adds to the height.

gridfinity.name: Gridfinity Master
gridfinity.desc: Parametric Gridfinity bins, baseplates and tool cutouts with STL and 3MF export.

startOver.title: Start over?
startOver.text: All settings of “{{mode}}” return to their defaults. Other modes, the language, the units and the export settings stay as they are. This cannot be undone.

site.motivation: Gridfinity is an open standard, and I believe the tools for it should be free too: no accounts, no paywalls, nothing to install. Everything runs in your browser. The other tools here (keychains, rack parts, photo cutouts) are things I make for myself and use myself, and I am simply sharing them.

footer.label: About this site
footer.donate: If PrintKit saved you time, you can say thanks with USDT on the TRON network (TRC20). Donations are optional.

consent.label: Analytics consent
consent.text: We would like to count visits to see how the site is used. This sets a cookie and sends page addresses and general visit data (browser, country) to an analytics service. Your photos, files and settings are never sent. Nothing is loaded until you accept.
